# Fix Flask page links

> check how the files is linked between each other becuase I keep not being able to open html pages from another html. It's python-flask whatever so might complicate things

<details><summary>10 previous messages</summary>

> I’ll trace the Flask routes, templates, and static links together so we can see where navigation is breaking. I’m going to start by mapping the project files and route definitions, then I’ll check the href/action/src paths against what Flask actually serves.
>
> A couple of things already stand out: Flask is serving route URLs like `/chat` and `/teacher-aura`, but several pages link to raw filenames like `/chat.html` or `/MyTeachersAura.html`. Also, `app.py` is trying to render files that are not currently in Flask’s `templates/` folder, which can cause `TemplateNotFound`. I’m reading the exact files now so I can make a clean routing fix instead of guessing.
>
> I found the main pattern: the project is half Flask routes and half “open this exact `.html` file” links, plus a couple of scripts still calling separate Node servers on ports `3000` and `3001`. I’m going to make Flask the single doorway: route aliases for the old `.html` URLs, correct template lookup for the existing folders, and local Flask API/static paths so the pages can open each other reliably.
>
> Before editing, here’s the actual breakage map: `app.py` currently has two Flask view functions both named `index`, which can prevent the app from starting; Flask only searches `templates/`, but routes point to `Game/testweb.html` and `MyTeacherAura/public/*.html`; and several links/scripts are written as filesystem-style paths instead of Flask routes/assets. I’m patching those together now.

Fixed the Flask linking setup. The main issue was that the app mixed Flask route URLs with raw `.html` file paths, and Flask was not configured to find templates in `Game/` or `MyTeacherAura/public/`.

What I changed:
- Updated [app.py](./app.py) so Flask can render templates from `templates/`, `Game/`, and `MyTeacherAura/public/`.
- Fixed duplicate Flask function names that could stop the app from starting.
- Added clean routes like `/index`, `/chat`, `/teacher-aura`, `/my-review`, `/review`.
- Kept old `.html` routes like `/chat.html` and `/Review.html` working too, so older links do not break.
- Replaced broken page links with `url_for(...)` in the HTML files.
- Moved teacher review API calls off `localhost:3001` and onto the Flask app.
- Fixed game links/assets so `Identity.py` and `pyscript.json` are served through Flask.

Verified:
- `python3 -m py_compile app.py`
- Flask test client returned `200` for all main pages, old `.html` aliases, scripts, and APIs.
- Browser click-through from `/index` to Study AI, Dashboard, My Reviews, and Kudos page worked.

To run it now:

```bash
python3 app.py
```

Then open:

```text
http://127.0.0.1:5001/index
```

- [MyTeachersAura.html](./MyTeacherAura/public/MyTeachersAura.html)
- [MyReview.html](./MyTeacherAura/public/MyReview.html)
- [Review.html](./MyTeacherAura/public/Review.html)
